turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hi! I'm Carla. My partner Miguel and I want to redo the kitchen in our Alvalade apartment. His parents are visiting in early May and we want it done before then. Where do we start?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Nice project. Early May gives about four months, which is realistic for a kitchen if decisions don't drag. Start with the budget and the layout; almost everything else follows from those two.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our total budget is €18,000, and we really can't go above it.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: €18,000 is workable for a mid-range kitchen in Lisbon if the layout stays mostly as it is. We'll treat it as a hard cap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How is a budget like that usually split?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Roughly: cabinets 25%, countertop 10–15%, labour 35–45%, appliances and tiles 15%, plus a contingency if you can. Labour is usually the biggest single line in Lisbon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For the layout, should we go L-shaped or galley?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That depends on the room. What are the dimensions, and where are the window and the door?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The window is on the short wall and the door is opposite it, so the long back wall is free.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then an L-shape along the back wall and the window wall works well: it keeps the door path clear and gives you the most counter space.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I measured the back wall: 3.40 m.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; the cabinet plan will be built around 3.40 m of run on that wall.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: IKEA or custom cabinets?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: With your budget, IKEA. Custom joinery for an L-shape would easily eat half the budget on its own.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I did the IKEA planner for Metod cabinets: €4,200 for the whole L.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's about 23% of the budget, right in range. Metod cabinets at €4,200 it is.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We asked two contractors for labour quotes. Ferreira Obras quoted €7,900.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's on the low end for demolition, plumbing, electrics and installation. Check what's excluded.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And Casa Nova Remodelações quoted €9,400, but as a fixed price, and they include waste removal.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A fixed price with waste removal is worth something: fewer surprises. €1,500 more, but with a firm number.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which one would you pick?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: On numbers alone Ferreira is cheaper. If the budget is truly tight, Ferreira, as long as the scope is written down.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We'll go with Ferreira Obras then.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: OK, Ferreira Obras. Get the quote itemised and signed before any work starts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Countertop: what material?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: For the look you described, quartz or a good stone-look laminate. Quartz is more durable; laminate is much cheaper.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We love quartz. The quote is €2,300 for both runs.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Quartz at €2,300 is about 13% of the budget, within range. Quartz it is.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We want the hob on the back wall instead of by the window. That means moving the gas line. Do we need a permit?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Moving a gas line is regulated work; it may need a comunicação prévia to the Câmara.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do I find out for sure?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ask the Câmara's urbanism desk or have the contractor check. Gas works also need a certified gas technician and an inspection afterwards.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sr. Ferreira came to measure properly: the back wall is actually 3.28 m, not 3.40. It's out of plumb and narrower at the top.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's 12 cm less than the plan assumes, which matters for the cabinet run.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: He also sent a revised quote: €2,100 extra 'for surprises', and he can only start in six weeks.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: An open-ended €2,100 'surprises' line on a quote you chose for being cheap removes its main advantage, and a six-week wait threatens the May deadline.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We're not comfortable with that. Should we drop Ferreira?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. Ferreira at €10,000 with an open-ended line is now more expensive than Casa Nova's fixed price, and slower.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then we go with Casa Nova?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes: Casa Nova Remodelações at their €9,400 fixed price [N_10]. Ana will be your project manager.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ana says they can start on 2 March.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 2 March leaves about eight weeks before early May, enough for a six-week job with some slack.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Because the wall is 3.28 m, the 40 cm drawer unit no longer fits. IKEA's planner suggests custom filler panels and a narrow custom unit. Cabinets go up to €5,100.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The 12 cm shortfall forces custom pieces, so the cabinet line rises from €4,200 to €5,100.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Where does that leave the total?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Cabinets €5,100 + labour €9,400 + quartz €2,300 + appliances and tiles about €2,900 = €19,700. That's €1,700 over the €18,000 cap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Idea: if we switch to an induction hob, there's no gas line to move at all. Does that also get rid of the permit question?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. With induction there's no gas work, so there's nothing to notify the Câmara about and no gas inspection. The permit question disappears. Switching to induction solves both problems.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ana says induction needs a dedicated circuit, so the electrician has to upgrade it: about €650.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a common requirement. It adds €650, so we need to keep an eye on the total.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So now we're at €20,350? Where can we cut?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, €20,350. The biggest flexible line is the countertop: a good stone-look laminate is around €800 versus €2,300 for quartz.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: OK. We'll switch the countertop from quartz to the stone-look HPL laminate.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That saves €1,500 and brings the total to €18,850. Still €850 over, but much closer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Miguel hates the idea. He says laminate will look cheap.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Modern HPL stone-look laminates are quite convincing, and they handle heat and scratches reasonably well. It's worth seeing a sample in person before deciding it looks cheap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: News: Miguel's parents offered to help. They're adding €3,500, so our budget is now €21,500.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's very generous, and it changes the picture: the budget is now €21,500.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So should we go back to quartz?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You could afford it now. But think about what else the margin could buy that you'd use more.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We talked it over. We'll keep the laminate and instead put the oven in a tall column cabinet at eye level, not under the hob. Miguel's mother has a bad back.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good use of the margin. A tall oven column adds about €900 for the cabinet and installation, and it's far more comfortable to use. Laminate stays.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you recap the whole budget now?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Cabinets €5,100 [N_22], labour with Casa Nova €9,400 [N_20], laminate €800 [N_27], appliances and tiles €2,900, circuit upgrade €650, oven column €900 [N_31]: €19,750 against a €21,500 budget, leaving €1,750 of contingency.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Bad news: the porcelain tiles are delayed two weeks, so Ana moved the start to 16 March.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 16 March instead of 2 March. That eats most of the slack before May.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Will it still be done before the visit in early May?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Let's check it against Casa Nova's schedule.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ana says it's a six-week job.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Six weeks from 16 March ends around 27 April. Tight, but it works, provided the cabinets and tiles arrive on time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good news: IKEA restocked a standard 30 cm Metod drawer unit. With it, the 3.28 m wall only needs a small standard filler, no custom pieces.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then drop the custom filler panels and the narrow custom unit. Cabinets come down to €4,600.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Demolition started today!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Exciting. The first few days usually reveal whatever is hiding behind the old cabinets.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: They found old cloth-insulated wiring behind the back wall. Ana says it has to be replaced: €1,100.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That has to be done; old cloth wiring is a fire risk. It comes out of the contingency.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Since the electrician is redoing the wiring anyway, does that change the induction circuit upgrade?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It might; ask him to check what the hob actually needs against what's there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The electrician checked: the existing 32A line to the hob position is enough for our induction hob. No upgrade needed.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: So the €650 circuit upgrade [N_25] is off the list; it partly offsets the rewiring.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Funny: Miguel told his parents on the phone that our '€18k kitchen' is coming along nicely. I didn't correct him.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Ha, that number stuck from the beginning. It's a good sign that things feel on track.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Tiling started. Do we tile the whole wall or just the backsplash?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Just the backsplash, up to the wall cabinets. Full-height tiling adds cost and time for little benefit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The cabinets are being installed. The small filler at the end of the 3.28 m wall looks fine.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; the standard filler works because the 30 cm unit absorbed most of the difference.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The oven column is in. Miguel's mother is going to love not bending down.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That was a good call. It's the change people use every single day.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We ran a bit short on tiles, since some broke. Ana says another box and fitting is €350.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Normal breakage. €350 is fine within the remaining contingency.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What colour should we paint the remaining walls?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A warm off-white goes well with the stone-look laminate and keeps the small room bright.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ana gave us the snag list: a drawer that doesn't close fully and a missing plinth.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Both are small. Make sure they're fixed before you sign off the final payment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Final bill: €20,050 in total.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That matches: the €19,750 plan, minus €500 on cabinets and the €650 upgrade you didn't need, plus €1,100 rewiring and €350 tiles. €20,050 against a €21,500 budget, €1,450 under.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Looking back, what did we change from our original plan, and why?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Four big changes. Contractor: Ferreira was dropped for an open-ended extra and a long wait [N_19], replaced by Casa Nova. Hob: induction instead of gas, which removed the permit issue [N_24]. Countertop: laminate instead of quartz to stay on budget [N_27]. Cabinets: back to a standard layout once IKEA restocked the 30 cm unit [N_36]. And the budget itself grew to €21,500.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Snags fixed, final payment made. The kitchen is done, two weeks before the visit!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations, Carla and Miguel. Finished before the visit and under budget.
